stories.headline: Nvidia CEO Says China AI Chip Market Share Dropped to Zero; US Senator Demands H200 Export Answers

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang told SCSP that Nvidia's market share of AI accelerators in China has 'now dropped to zero', down from 95% before export controls began
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said that the company's market share of AI accelerators in China has now dropped to 0%.

key_facts.fact: Huang said US export policy 'has already largely backfired' and called abandoning a market the size of China strategically unsound
key_facts.excerpt: US export restrictions bite. … Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said that the company's market share of AI accelerators in China has now dropped to 0%.

key_facts.fact: Sen. Chris Coons pressed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick about contradictions regarding H200 chip sales to China in a letter reported May 3
key_facts.excerpt: Sen. Chris Coons, D-Del., pressed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick about allowing Nvidia's H200 chips for artificial intelligence to be sold to China in a letter first reported by CNBC.

key_facts.fact: Lutnick told April 22 hearing 'We have not sold them any chips as of yet,' contradicting Huang's March statement that Nvidia got approvals from both US and Chinese governments to sell H200 chips to China
key_facts.excerpt: Lutnick's statement contradicted remarks from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who told reporters in March that Nvidia had gotten approvals from both the US and Chinese government to sell H200 chips to China.

key_facts.fact: Bernstein had predicted Nvidia's China AI GPU share would drop from 66% in 2024 to ~8%, but actual decline was far more dramatic according to Huang
key_facts.excerpt: 伯恩斯坦（Bernstein）曾預測輝達在中國AI GPU市佔率可能從2024年的66%降到未來幾年的8%左右，不過根據黃仁勳的說法，下降趨勢比預期更劇烈。

key_facts.fact: Huawei's AI chip market share in China now exceeds 50%, with projections of 60% growth in 2026, filling the void Nvidia left
key_facts.excerpt: Huawei is positioned to capitalize on this shift, with projections indicating that sales of Huawei's AI chips will increase by 60% by 2026.

key_facts.fact: Coons asked Lutnick to respond within one week with how many H200 chips received export licenses, how many shipped, and how many more the Commerce Department plans to license
key_facts.excerpt: Coons also asked Lutnick to respond in the next week with how many H200 chips received licenses for export to China, how many have been shipped to China and how many more the Commerce Department plans to license.

stories.headline: Cerebras Begins IPO Roadshow Seeking Up to $26.6B Valuation, Aims to Raise $3.5B

key_facts.fact: Cerebras is aiming to sell 28 million shares at $115-$125 apiece, seeking a valuation of up to $26.62 billion
key_facts.excerpt: AI chipmaker Cerebras Systems, a rival to Nvidia, is scheduled to kick off its IPO roadshow on Monday, with shares expected to be priced between $115 and $125.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg sources say Cerebras could target up to $40 billion valuation and raise as much as $4 billion, with banks receiving $10B+ in indications of interest
key_facts.excerpt: The banks on the deal have already received indications of interest in excess of $10 billion worth of potential orders.

key_facts.fact: This is Cerebras' second attempt to go public after withdrawing its previous IPO filing last October
key_facts.excerpt: This marks Cerebras' second attempt to go public after withdrawing a previous IPO filing last October.

key_facts.fact: Revenue rose to $510 million in 2025 (up from $290.3M), with profit of $1.38/share versus a loss of $9.90/share a year earlier
key_facts.excerpt: The company's revenue rose to $510 million in the year ended December 31, up from $290.3 million a year earlier. It also reported a profit of $1.38 per share, a turnaround from a loss of $9.90 per share a year earlier.

key_facts.fact: Cerebras struck a multi-year deal with OpenAI valued at $20B+, under which OpenAI will deploy 750 MW of Cerebras's high-speed AI compute
key_facts.excerpt: Cerebras, which had been reliant on business from G42… Cerebras had struck a multi-year deal with OpenAI valued at more than $20 billion.

key_facts.fact: In February 2026, Cerebras raised $1 billion at $23 billion valuation led by Tiger Global, with AMD, Benchmark, Fidelity, Altimeter, and Coatue as investors
key_facts.excerpt: In February, Cerebras raised about $1 billion in a funding round that valued the firm at $23 billion including money raised. The funding was led by Tiger Global Management with participation from investors including Benchmark, Fidelity Management & Research Co., and Advanced Micro Devices.

key_facts.fact: Morgan Stanley, Citigroup, Barclays, and UBS are lead underwriters; company plans to list on Nasdaq under ticker 'CBRS'
key_facts.excerpt: The company now aims to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol 'CBRS'. Morgan Stanley, Citigroup, Barclays and UBS are the lead underwriters for the offering.

stories.headline: China's Linkerbot Closes $3B Series B+, Targets $6B With 80%+ Global Robotic Hands Share

key_facts.fact: Beijing-based Linkerbot completed a 'Series B+' funding round last week valued at $3 billion, and will seek $6 billion in its next round
key_facts.excerpt: Linkerbot completed what it called a 'series B+' funding round last week that valued it at $3 billion.

key_facts.fact: Linkerbot holds over 80% of the global market share in high-degree-of-freedom (DoF) robotic hands, the only firm shipping above 1,000 units per month
key_facts.excerpt: Reuters describes Linkerbot as the global market leader in high-degree-of-freedom dexterous hands, with more than 80 per cent share by volume and the only operation in the world capable of shipping above 1,000 units a month.

key_facts.fact: Plans to scale production from roughly 5,000 units per month to 10,000 units per month
key_facts.excerpt: Linkerbot currently holds over 80% of the global market share in high-degree-of-freedom (DoF) robotic hands, and plans to scale production 'soon' to 10,000 units a month from almost 5,000 currently.

key_facts.fact: Early backers include Alibaba's Ant Group and Sequoia spin-off HongShan Group; latest round added Zhongguancun Science Park Fund, Bank of China Asset Management, and Fosun Capital
key_facts.excerpt: Prominent early backers of the two-year-old unicorn include Alibaba's Ant Group and Sequoia spin-off HongShan Group, while the state-backed Zhongguancun Science Park Fund, Bank of China Asset Management and Fosun Capital participated in the latest round.

key_facts.fact: Two-year-old company with 400+ employees and five factories across Beijing and Shenzhen, some designed as intelligent production lines where robotic hands assemble more robotic hands
key_facts.excerpt: Reuters reports more than 400 employees and five factories across Beijing and Shenzhen. The most quietly ambitious detail… is that some of those factories are being designed as intelligent production lines on which Linkerbot's robotic hands assemble more robotic hands.

key_facts.fact: Linkerbot's hands can rapidly turn screws, grasp deformable soft objects, thread a needle, and perform high-precision manufacturing, with a 500+ dexterous skill dataset called LinkerSkillNet
key_facts.excerpt: Linkerbot's hands can already rapidly turn screws, grasp deformable soft objects, thread a needle and engage in high-precision manufacturing.

key_facts.fact: Humanoid robot costs remain $100K-$150K per unit for leading industrial models from Unitree, AgiBot, and UBTech; Unitree filed for Shanghai IPO in March at up to $7B valuation
key_facts.excerpt: A major obstacle to the widespread factory use of humanoids is their cost, at $100,000 to $150,000 per unit for the leading industrial models from Unitree, AgiBot and UBTech.

stories.headline: EU's €20B AI Gigafactory Plan Faces Criticism Over Demand Doubts and Nvidia GPU Dependency

key_facts.fact: European Commission plans €20 billion for 4-5 AI gigafactories with 100,000+ GPUs each, forming Europe's answer to OpenAI's $500B Stargate project
key_facts.excerpt: Commission President Ursula von der Leyen outlined the ambition in February last year, proposing four to five mega computing facilities, each powered by 100,000 GPUs, forming Europe's answer to OpenAI's 500 billion dollar Stargate project.

key_facts.fact: 76 bids for 60 sites across 16 countries were filed, but legislators and experts question whether actual demand exists for the compute capacity
key_facts.excerpt: A total of 76 bids for 60 sites across 16 countries were filed during an informal sense-check last year. But legislators and experts say which companies would use this computing power remains unclear.

key_facts.fact: A group of 18 European Parliament lawmakers warned the Commission about dependency on Nvidia as a single chip supplier, questioning how the plan reduces strategic dependencies
key_facts.excerpt: A group of 18 European Parliament lawmakers warned the Commission about dependency on a single chip supplier, questioning how the gigafactory initiative would reduce Europe's strategic dependencies.

key_facts.fact: Mistral is not waiting for gigafactories: announced $1.2B data center in Sweden in February and raised hundreds of millions for a Paris facility in March
key_facts.excerpt: Europe's most prominent AI developer, Mistral, isn't waiting for the gigafactories. In February, it announced a 1.2 billion dollar data center investment in Sweden. At the end of March, it raised hundreds of millions of euros for a facility near Paris.

key_facts.fact: Commission defended plan as about 'sovereign compute' with data 'fully protected under European law, without the possibility of third country interference'
key_facts.excerpt: The Commission's spokesperson Thomas Regnier pushed back. 'This is not just about raw compute power, it's about sovereign compute,' he said.

key_facts.fact: Siemens warned EU regulations are pushing its AI spending outside Europe; financing model requires 65% from private parties, already causing delays
key_facts.excerpt: Siemens recently warned that EU regulations are pushing its AI spending outside Europe… the gigafactory financing model requires 65 percent from private parties, and that structure is already causing delays in some member states.

sources.title: EU's €20B AI gigafactory plan faces growing backlash

stories.headline: Nvidia's Asian Suppliers Now ~90% of Production Costs, Up From 65%, as Ties Shift to Physical AI

key_facts.fact: Asian suppliers account for about 90% of Nvidia's production costs, up from roughly 65% last year, according to Bloomberg data
key_facts.excerpt: Asian suppliers account for about 90 percent of Nvidia's production costs, up from about 65 percent last year, data compiled by Bloomberg showed.

key_facts.fact: In the past week alone, LG Electronics, Nanya Technology, Desay SV, and Pateo Connect rallied on news of Nvidia tie-ups, supply-chain participation, or product collaboration
key_facts.excerpt: Just in the past week, South Korea's LG Electronics Inc, Taiwan's Nanya Technology Corp, as well as China's Huizhou Desay SV Automotive Co and Pateo Connect Technology Shanghai Corp have become the latest to rally on news of tie-ups.

key_facts.fact: Latest wave of collaborations shifts beyond semiconductors into physical AI, including robotics, autonomous systems, and AI-enabled manufacturing
key_facts.excerpt: The latest wave of collaborations in the region pointed to a shift beyond semiconductors into physical AI.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia accounts for roughly half of Microsoft's capex and about one-quarter of Amazon's, with a smaller but still leading share at Meta and Alphabet
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia accounts for about half of Microsoft's capital expenditure and roughly one-quarter of Amazon's, with a smaller but still leading share at Meta and Alphabet.

key_facts.fact: Core partnerships deepened through chip-focused ties with TSMC, SK Hynix, and Samsung; hyperscalers committed $190B-$200B each in 2026 capex (Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet) and up to $145B (Meta)
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon.com Inc, Microsoft Corp and Alphabet Inc each committing about US$190 billion to US$200 billion for this year, and Meta Platforms Inc raising its outlays to as much as US$145 billion.

stories.headline: SoftBank Plans to Produce Lithium- and Cobalt-Free Data Center Batteries in Japan by FY2027

key_facts.fact: SoftBank Group will seek to make batteries that do not require expensive lithium and cobalt in Japan, targeting production as soon as FY2027
key_facts.excerpt: TOKYO — Japan's SoftBank Group will seek to make batteries that do not require expensive lithium and cobalt in Japan…

key_facts.fact: The initiative is part of Japan's broader push to reduce reliance on Chinese-controlled metal supply chains for critical minerals
key_facts.excerpt: SoftBank aims to make data center batteries without lithium, cobalt

key_facts.fact: Batteries are intended for data center use, connecting SoftBank's energy strategy to its AI infrastructure ambitions including the $33B Piketon power plant and $500B Stargate partnership
